gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both concern tangential dynamics and inter-mode generation, but ISSUE-002 diagnoses applying a center-local derivative bound and Gronwall without ensuring continued residence in a fixed center region. Gold instead identifies the insufficiency of even the stated conditional second-moment bound and approximate motion equation to characterize the tangent-space distribution or determine the appearance of inter-mode probability. Neither this prediction nor another supplied entry recognizes that distinct inferential overclaim.

ISSUE-003 diagnoses a small eigengap at center-dominated points and the unsupported theta-small time derivative of a theoretical tangent frame. Gold concerns early high-noise MNIST measurements, where anisotropic eigengaps collapse as a_t tends to zero, making the plotted normal-distance interpretation unreliable without a spectral reliability check. An eigengap assumption at centers does not recognize this different limiting regime or the experimental interpretation obligation. No supplied prediction diagnoses the full gold concern.

ISSUE-007 challenges global reach and third-derivative bounds used to justify theoretical projection geometry. Gold concerns the numerical estimator accepting normal-score zeros without checking the defining negative-curvature condition lambda_{d*+1} <= -beta. Bounding reach on the whole ridge does not identify or repair acceptance of stationary points outside that ridge. None of the supplied entries explicitly recognizes the missing candidate curvature test.

ISSUE-003 addresses an unsupported time-derivative estimate for the tangent frame at centers, caused by a small spectral gap. Gold instead identifies omission of the spatial product-rule term (DE[delta])^T grad log p from the Newton Jacobian of F = E^T grad log p. Re-estimating frame motion under an eigengap assumption does not recognize that omitted Jacobian contribution. No supplied prediction diagnoses the Hessian-only Newton formula or supplies the full product-rule repair.

ISSUE-003 requires separation between Hessian eigenvalues to control a tangent-frame derivative at centers. Gold requires selected eigenvalues themselves to be bounded away from zero before applying Lambda_perp(x)^{-1} at unrestricted estimator inputs. A small eigengap can coexist with nonzero eigenvalues, and an eigengap assumption does not ensure invertibility. No supplied entry identifies the raw inverse's domain failure or gives a minimum-magnitude, conditioning, or damped-solve safeguard for this estimator.
